title: JobPhases
description: Data file content/jobs/phases.json: which phases of the game day are the compute night of the AI service (B7 S4, D471 D4). The core signals the change from the world calendar, so it is the same in every run.

night_day_phases.description: Day phases (vocabulary time_of_day) that count as compute night.

not_before_minute.description: A1798 (Marcel W2243, B2839): the compute night does not begin before this minute of the day (1410 = 23:30), even when all sleep earlier and also not at the latest-start limit - those awake live their evening until then. A minute that lies more than 12 hours after nightfall does not hold. Omitted = from nightfall, as before.

wait_for_sleepers_hours.description: B2680 (Marcel W1939): the compute night begins when every inhabitant sleeps, at the latest this many game hours after nightfall (the start of the first night phase); the night scene of the game waits the same (look/night.json wait_for_sleepers_max_h). Omitted = at nightfall, as before.

night_queue.description: A1766 (A1568 step 2b, B2789, D1113 v3 4b): with the player's day mode 'night_only' the jobs of these kinds are not sent by day but held in the save game's night queue, and sent when the compute night begins - most important first (the job's own priority plus a bonus per night it waited), the oldest and each inhabitant in turn, at most cap_per_night; the rest waits for the next night, never dropped. Switching back to 'ai' sends what waits at once. Omitted = nothing is held.

held_kinds.description: Job kinds (generation-job kind) held by day in night_only; the night kinds (question, memory, review, dream, chronicle) go at night anyway, a talk (dialogue) belongs to its moment and is not sent by day at all.

cap_per_night.description: Jobs sent from the queue per compute night at most (placeholder 24 for 4 inhabitants).

age_bonus_per_night.description: Priority added per night a job waited, so what is left over moves up.
